claims.statement: For each fixed path-star profile, branch i, and coefficient j, expanding B_(r_h)=L^r_h+z in H_i yields the reported subset/epsilon/s binomial identity for T_i[j]. Retaining subsets of size at most d gives U_i^(d)[j]<=T_i[j] because all omitted coefficient terms are nonnegative.
claims.scope: Exact algebraic identity and coefficient lower bound for fixed ordinary path-star profiles with original branch arities and multiplicities. No uniform local three-halves bound, selector theorem, selected MASS, or exact-ratio payment is implied.
claims.reason: Direct expansion of each B factor proves the identity; coefficient nonnegativity proves the truncation inequality.

Both selectors are strict on every listed row, and full T_i passes the tested rows.
claims.scope: Bounded exact evidence for only the two stated profiles and their actual eligible ranks. Not a universal local coefficient theorem, full local-mass counterexample, selected MASS result, or payment result. Original private-tip multiplicities remain four per branch.
claims.reason: The producer implementation sets F=[1,1,1] at r=4, whereas the contract gives F4=(3,3,1). Independent exact convolution corrects the m=40 layer margins; the stated m=150 truncation outcomes remain valid.
